title: Image Grading: eccentricity max can be set to 1.00, which is a threshold the pipeline can never exceed - the check becomes inert with no warning
what_happened: I typed 5 into 'Eccentricity max'; it clamped to 1.00 and persisted image_grading_eccentricity_threshold=1.0. Frame eccentricity is computed as sqrt(1 - lambda2/lambda1), which is strictly < 1.0 for any star with a finite minor axis, and the rule is 'reject if eccentricity exceeds this value' - so 1.00 can never fire. The UI gives no indication that the check is now dead. The same shape applies at the other end of several ranges: HFR absolute min 0.1 px (below any achievable HFR -> rejects every frame), HFR absolute max 50 px (never fires), star-count min max 100000 (rejects every frame on any realistic sensor).
expected: Clamp eccentricity to something the detector can actually exceed (e.g. 0.99), or annotate the field when the value makes the check inert ('at 1.00 this check never fires'). Same for the HFR/star-count extremes.
repro: Settings > Imaging > Image Grading: enable the master toggle, click 'Eccentricity max', Ctrl+A, type 5, Enter -> field shows 1.00, DB shows 1.0.
proposed_fix: Cap at 0.99 and surface an inline note when a threshold is outside the range the pipeline can produce.
verdict_reasoning: Mechanically reproduced: enabled the master toggle, typed 5 into 'Eccentricity max' -> field clamps to 1.00 and sqlite image_grading_eccentricity_threshold=1.0 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-43-ecc.png). UI range confirmed at image_grading_settings.dart:196-197 (min 0.0 / max 1.0); the other cited ranges are also as claimed (HFR absolute min 0.1 / max 50 at :150-151, star count min 1 / max 100000 at :217-218). The inertness holds, but NOT via the file the finding cites: difference_image.rs:865-876 moment_eccentricity is the transient-detection measure, not the grading path. The grading value is stats.rs:526 (sqrt(1 - lambda2/lambda1)) aggregated by frame_eccentricity (stats.rs:957-963), which explicitly filters to (0.0..=1.0), and image_grading.rs:200-201 compares 'ecc > threshold' - so at 1.00 the gate can never fire. Severity corrected P3 -> P4: 1.00 is the mathematical maximum of the metric, the field already documents 'Leave blank to disable', and clamping out-of-range input to the legal maximum is standard behaviour. This is a copy/annotation nit, not a defect that can cost data.

title: Sequence checkpoints and logs are written to the platform app-support directory, ignoring the configured data directory
unit: settings:captured-images (observed while auditing; owner is the sequencer/storage layer)
what_happened: With SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR both pointed at /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/data, the app logged 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' and 'Log directory: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs'. skotiq_session.checkpoint in that shared directory was being rewritten by my sandboxed instance. The visible consequence: on entering the app I was offered 'Recover Sequence? ... New Sequence, Saved 0m ago, Completed 6 frames (0m integration)' for a sequence that does not exist in this profile's database (select * from sequence_checkpoints returned zero rows).
expected: Checkpoint and log paths must follow the same data-directory resolution as the database, so a second profile/data-dir never reads or overwrites another instance's run state.
repro: Start the app with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR set to a scratch path; read /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/app.log for the two 'directory' lines; ls -la ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/ shows skotiq_session.checkpoint mtime tracking the sandboxed run.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/app.log lines at 13:54:14 ('Log directory: ...') and 13:54:15 ('Setting checkpoint directory to: ...'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-04-skip.png (the phantom Recover dialog); sqlite3 output 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> empty
where: source-only beyond the log lines - the checkpoint-directory call site is in the native bridge startup path, not in my area's Dart files
proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint and log roots from the same SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware helper the database uses.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently in my own fresh instance. /proc/1436364/environ confirms SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging-verify/data, yet that instance's own log says 'Log directory: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs' (15:10:40) and 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' (15:10:41). The visible consequence reproduced too: immediately after 'Skip onboarding' the app offered 'Recover Sequence? ... AUDIT SEQ, Saved 0m ago, Completed 2 frames' (siv-02-skip.png) for a sequence that does not exist in this profile - sqlite 'select count(*) from sequence_checkpoints' returns 0. The dialog is modal and Escape does not dismiss it, so the only exits are Resume (would run another instance's sequence) or Discard (I backed the shared file up first, clicked Discard, and restored it - which also proves the write side of the hazard). CORRECTION to the finding's 'where': the call site is NOT in the native bridge startup path, it is Dart - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 calls backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir(supportDir.path) with getApplicationSupportDirectory(), and apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60-68 pins the log dir the same way (configureSkotiqDataDirectory only fills SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when it is unset, and the logDir/checkpoint paths never consult it at all). Severity P2 stands: for a single desktop instance the practical impact is only that a relocated data directory is not honoured, but the project documents running a headless daemon alongside a GUI on one host (main_headless with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR), and in that supported configuration the two processes share one checkpoint file.
